Subject: RetailCo trial charter and model selection — next steps

Hi Carlos,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion and lots of clarity on your main goals. Quick recap from our side and proposed POC (trial) charter to keep momentum: 

Summary of goals
- Improve automated answers in the store policy chatbot (reduce handoffs to agents by 40% for policy/returns questions)
- Maintain answer quality for Spanish customers (current volume ~18% of queries)
- Keep 95th percentile latency under 450ms for single-turn answers in peak traffic

Proposed success criteria (measurable)
- Reduction in human escalation rate from policy intents by >=40% within 6 weeks of trial
- Precision@1 on a labeled 200-case prompt set >= 85% (bilingual: EN/ES)
- 95th percentile response latency <= 450ms at target QPS (details below)

Evaluation plan & timeline
1) Week 0 (kickoff): finalize dataset and access — you provide 2k representative queries + 200 labeled eval cases (we can redact PII).
2) Week 1: baseline run on current production model (RetailCo baseline) + initial runs for two open model candidates.
3) Week 2–3: fine-tune / instruction-tune narrow prompt patterns where needed; run multilingual checks.
4) Week 4–5: load testing and latency tuning, rollout to canary (internal agents) then public beta.
5) Week 6: finalize evaluation, handoff to ops for production plan or next steps.

Ownership
- Redwood: project lead Ben Carter (technical lead), Marissa Cole (model configuration & eval), Rachel Kim (program owner / escalation).
- RetailCo: Carlos (Product), Samantha (Ops), Procurement for PO path.

Model recommendation for trial (initial shortlist)
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-Chat-8B (open-instruct optimized) — good instruction-following and cost profile for short answers.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B (quantized) — robust for longer context when we hit edge cases; slower but compatible with our fallback routing.
- Multilingual handling: run bilingual prompt templates + small Spanish instruction-tuning pass (100–300 examples) if baseline EN->ES performance is below threshold.

Resources and constraints
- Target QPS for canary: 8 QPS steady-state, burst to 20 QPS for load tests.
- Data retention: Redwood logs request IDs for tracing only; full utterances stored under agreed SOW (we'll respect your retention policy).

Next steps I recommend this week
- Carlos: confirm you can share the 2k query sample and the 200 labeled eval cases (or indicate timeline).
- Procurement: share PO instructions / standard SOW redlines (cc'd if easier).
- Ben/Marissa: I'll have Ben draft the SOW and Marissa will prepare a model matrix for your review.

Attachments: RetailCo_POC_Charter_v1.pdf (POC charter), model_matrix_retailco.xlsx (initial comparisons), SOW_trial_scope_v1.docx (draft scope).

Happy to adjust — if all looks good I propose we kick week 0 on Monday 2027-03-08.

Thanks,

Hi Carlos — thanks for the quick turnaround. Short answers to your questions and next pieces from Redwood: 

Q1 — Spanish instruction tuning: 100 example pairs (user prompt + ideal response) is a reasonable starting point for a light instruction pass that often moves accuracy by ~6–10 points on targeted intents. For bigger gains, 300–500 examples is better. For your timeline I'd say 150–200 is a pragmatic tradeoff.

Q2 — Data masking: please remove any PII before transfer. If you cannot, we can accept files in our secure S3 with encryption but must have a brief data processing addendum (we'll send a template). For eval cases we prefer minimal context — just the user utterance, language tag, and expected canonical answer.

Model matrix excerpt (attached spreadsheet has more detail):
- Mistral-Instruct-Chat-8B: fast, low cost, strong short-answer instruction tuning; recommended starting point.
- Llama-2-13B (int8 quantized): keeps robustness for unusual edge-case policy questions; plan to route ~5–10% of calls to this model as a fallback during the trial for hard cases.
- OpenAssistant-13B: alternative if you need better long-form synthesis but cost is higher — we can deprioritize unless you expect multi-turn escalation answers.

Proposed trial billing approach: fixed trial credit for the 6-week period covering model evaluation + a small per-token overage clause. We will draft the order form to match your procurement preference.

Next actions I am putting on my plate this morning:
- Draft SOW/order form + send data-processing addendum template (by EOD Tue 2027-03-02).
- Marissa to run a short sandbox with a synthetic subset once we get the 2k sample.

I'll attach the SOW and model matrix to the shared drive (links in the charter).

—Ben
